purpose: Periodic table reference, keyed by element symbol so other files can store {"element_ref": "Fe"} instead of duplicating numeric data. Sourced from CIAAW/IUPAC-aligned open data (Bowserinator/Periodic-Table-JSON), covering all 118 confirmed elements.
conventions: atomic_mass_u for elements with no stable isotopes is the mass number of the longest-lived known isotope (IUPAC convention), not a natural-abundance-weighted average.

null means the property has not been experimentally measured or does not apply in the usual sense -- not that it is zero. Superheavy elements (Z > 100) are synthesized one atom at a time with sub-second half-lives, so many bulk properties (density, melting/boiling point) are genuinely unmeasured.
null melting_point_K for C, P, As reflects real physical complexity (sublimation, multiple allotropes) at standard pressure, not missing data.
electronegativity_pauling is null for elements too reactive/short-lived to measure, and for most noble gases where the concept doesn't meaningfully apply.
ionization_energies_kJ_per_mol is a list, first value = first ionization energy, second = second, etc. -- as many as have been measured.

He.name: Helium
He.appearance: colorless gas, exhibiting a red-orange glow when placed in a high-voltage electric field

Ne.name: Neon
Ne.appearance: colorless gas exhibiting an orange-red glow when placed in a high voltage electric field

P.name: Phosphorus
P.appearance: colourless, waxy white, yellow, scarlet, red, violet, black

Ar.name: Argon
Ar.appearance: colorless gas exhibiting a lilac/violet glow when placed in a high voltage electric field

Fe.name: Iron
Fe.appearance: lustrous metallic with a grayish tinge

Ni.name: Nickel
Ni.appearance: lustrous, metallic, and silver with a gold tinge

Se.name: Selenium
Se.appearance: black, red, and gray (not pictured) allotropes

Kr.name: Krypton
Kr.appearance: colorless gas, exhibiting a whitish glow in a high electric field

I.name: Iodine
I.appearance: lustrous metallic gray, violet as a gas

Xe.name: Xenon
Xe.appearance: colorless gas, exhibiting a blue glow when placed in a high voltage electric field

Rn.name: Radon
Rn.appearance: colorless gas, occasionally glows green or red in discharge tubes

Pu.name: Plutonium
Pu.appearance: silvery white, tarnishing to dark gray in air

Cm.name: Curium
Cm.appearance: silvery metallic, glows purple in the dark
